Package com.nexuslink.security.vault

Class VaultBackupService

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.security.vault.VaultBackupService
public final class VaultBackupService extends Object
Produces and restores portable, passphrase-encrypted backups of a CredentialVault.

A backup is intentionally distinct from the live vault file written by VaultStore: it can be written to any path, carries a small self-describing header (format id, schema version, creation timestamp) so future versions can migrate it, and is re-encrypted under a backup passphrase that is independent of the vault's own master password.

This service is a thin orchestration layer — it owns no cryptography. Entries are re-encrypted by handing plaintext to a fresh CredentialVault created with the backup passphrase, so all AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2 logic continues to live in CredentialVault. Import verifies the passphrase (and integrity, via the GCM authentication tag) before returning; a wrong passphrase or a tampered/corrupt file always fails with VaultBackupException rather than yielding a partial vault.

  • Method Details

    • exportBackup

      public void exportBackup(CredentialVault vault, Path destination, char[] passphrase) throws VaultBackupException
      Export an encrypted, self-contained backup of vault to destination.

      The source vault must be unlocked: its secrets are read in the clear and re-encrypted under passphrase, so the resulting file can later be opened with that passphrase regardless of the vault's original master password.

      Throws:
      VaultBackupException - if the backup cannot be written
      CredentialVault.VaultException - if vault is locked

    • importBackup

      public CredentialVault importBackup(Path source, char[] passphrase) throws VaultBackupException
      Read and decrypt a backup from source, returning a fully reconstructed, unlocked CredentialVault.
      Throws:
      VaultBackupException - if the file is missing/unreadable, is not a recognised backup, has an unsupported version, has been tampered with, or the passphrase is wrong

    • restoreInto

      public int restoreInto(CredentialVault target, Path source, char[] passphrase, boolean overwriteExisting) throws VaultBackupException
      Import a backup and merge its entries into an existing, unlocked target vault.

      For each backed-up reference, if target already holds that key the entry is only replaced when overwriteExisting is true; otherwise the existing value is kept. Keys absent from target are always added.

      Returns:
      the number of entries written into target
      Throws:
      VaultBackupException - if the backup cannot be imported (see importBackup(java.nio.file.Path, char[]))
